Quotes / Karl Popper / Q0131

English

We may become the makers of our fate when we have ceased to pose as its prophets.
Thinker Karl Popper
School Critical Rationalism
Source The Open Society and Its Enemies
Theme Fate

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with The Open Society and Its Enemies, within the tradition of Critical Rationalism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of fate, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Karl Popper's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
